hypothesis: This distinct T2 variant tests whether locating the first high-bit lane from the SIMD mask is cheaper than the parent’s scalar byte-by-byte scan of a mixed 16-byte block. SIMD still skips only complete ASCII blocks; the first high-bit byte, including a possible stray continuation, is passed to the existing strict scalar decoder. Loads remain bounded by n. It is not T1 whole-buffer validation or a hybrid; the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and ASCII/malformed boundary checks must determine whether it helps.
notes: The parent result is valid but slower than the measured baseline; no new performance or correctness result is claimed here. The controller should evaluate this mask-lane lookup on the official mixed-width workload and boundary-focused correctness suite.
transformations: In the existing SSE2 ASCII-run scanner, use a four-step binary subdivision of the movemask to return the first high-bit lane directly instead of falling back to byte-by-byte source scanning within that vector block.
Leave the strict scalar UTF-8 decoder, scalar tail handling, ABI, output, and thread budget unchanged.
